title: Two Ends of the Map
premise: Two travelers each hold half a route map, but each half is unreadable alone and they refuse to let go of their section. They walk side by side to align the torn edges, discover the destination lies between their starting points, and turn together.
hook: We each have half the answer.
visible_action: Map halves slide and rotate; torn edges meet; a dotted route crosses the seam; both travelers pivot in unison.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Combining partial information can change the plan.
gate: Use an invented location and map; do not imply a real navigation route.

editorial_pick.original_reason: Split map knowledge supports a clear cooperation story and a useful matched-view composition.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Start with each character holding one map portion. Reveal the combined route through shared action.
editorial_pick.gate: Keep the map geometry consistent and ensure cooperation, rather than a lucky coincidence, resolves the obstacle.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
